title: Sales Purchase Agreement (SPA) in UAE – Key Insights & Legal Guide
description: Learn all about the Sales Purchase Agreement in the UAE, including key elements and essential clauses for secure transactions.

contentHtml:
A Sales Purchase Agreement is a legally binding contract. SPA outlines the terms and conditions of good’s sale and purchase. Including the sale and purchase of property, or services. This agreement is fundamental. Especially in establishing clear expectations. Meanwhile, protecting the rights of parties involved in the transaction.

In the UAE, SPAs have a major role in business and real estate transactions. It offers security and clarity in agreements. The blog is written to talk about SPA in detail. Let’s begin exploring detail and understand what a Sales Purchase Agreement is about and how it works.

What is a Sales Purchase Agreement (SPA)

An SPA is a vital document. It serves as the foundation of any transaction. This involves the sale of assets or goods. Be it real estate or commercial businesses. Other high-value transactions are also part of it. This agreement ensures that all parties involved have an understanding of their rights and obligations. It helps in mitigating risks and preventing disputes. Also, establishing legal recourse in case of any breaches.

In the UAE, SPAs are commonly used in:

  • Real estate deals
  • Business sales, and
  • Corporate mergers or
  • Acquisitions.

Understanding the details of an SPA is essential. Especially for anyone engaging in these transaction types.

Understanding the Importance of an SPA

The importance of an SPA lies in the protection it offers to both parties in a transaction. Below are the reasons why having an SPA is crucial:

  1. Legal Protection: It’s a legally enforceable document. It outlines the responsibilities and rights of the buyer and seller.
  2. Clarity of Terms: It provides a clear understanding of the transaction’s terms. This prevents misunderstandings.
  3. Mitigation of Risks: An SPA helps in identifying potential risks. It establishes mechanisms to mitigate them.
  4. Dispute Resolution: The SPA includes provisions for resolving any disputes. Those disputes may arise through arbitration/legal channels.

Key Elements of a Sales Purchase Agreement

Legal Framework Governing SPAs in the UAE

The UAE legal framework surrounding SPAs is governed by UAE Federal Law No. 5 of 1985.

  • The Civil Transactions Law)
  • The UAE Commercial Code, and
  • Specific real estate regulations.

The SPA is subject to local regulations in the respective emirate for real estate transactions. It can be Dubai or Abu Dhabi.

Real Estate Law:

When an SPA involves real estate, it is further governed by the relevant local regulations. Especially in cities like Dubai. This includes:

  • The Dubai Land Department (DLD) laws and
  • RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Agency) guidelines.

Commercial Law:

The SPA is governed by the UAE Commercial Code for business/commercial transactions. It addresses:

  • Business mergers
  • Acquisitions, and
  • The sale of commercial assets.

Types of Sales Purchase Agreements in the UAE

In the UAE, there are several types of SPAs. It depends on the transaction’s nature. The following are the common types:

Real Estate SPA: Used when buying or selling property, often detailing aspects such as land title transfer, payment schedules, and obligations of both parties.

Business SPA: Applied in the sale of a business. It includes:

  • Assets
  • Goodwill, or
  • Shares of a company

It often includes warranties and non-compete clauses.

Goods and Services SPA: Involving the sale of tangible or intangible goods. Along with detailing delivery terms, warranties, and after-sales services.

How to Draft a Sales Purchase Agreement

Drafting an SPA requires careful attention to detail. As a result, it ensures all essential elements are included. This way, both parties’ interests are protected. The process typically involves:

  1. Identifying the Parties: Identify the buyer and the seller.
  2. Describing the Asset: Provide a detailed description of the asset/goods being sold.
  3. Agreeing on Payment Terms: Specify the price and payment schedule. Along with any deposit requirements.
  4. Outlining Deliverables: Define when and how the goods or property will be delivered or transferred.
  5. Including Legal Clauses: Incorporate warranties, conditions precedent, termination rights, and dispute resolution mechanisms.
  6. Reviewing Local Regulations: Ensure the SPA complies with relevant UAE laws and industry-specific regulations.

Common Terms & Clauses in an SPA

In any SPA, some commonly used terms and clauses that should be considered are:

  1. Deposit Clause: Specifies any advance payments or security deposits. It is required of the buyer.
  2. Force Majeure: Defines the conditions under which a party may be excused. Specifically, from fulfilling their obligations due to unforeseen circumstances. An example included is natural disasters.
  3. Non-Compete Clause: Common in business SPAs. This clause prevents the seller from competing with the buyer. Particularly in a specific industry or region.
  4. Confidentiality Clause: Ensures that parties maintain confidentiality. Regarding the transaction details.

SPA for Real Estate Transactions in the UAE

In the UAE, real estate transactions are among the most common uses of SPAs. The SPA outlines the terms for transferring property ownership. It assures that both parties are clear on their obligations. In the case of a real estate transaction, the SPA includes:

  • A detailed description of the property.
  • The agreed-upon sale price and payment structure.
  • A timeline for transferring the title of the property.
  • Compliance with the relevant laws and regulations of the specific emirate.

SPA for Business and Commercial Deals

In business deals, an SPA may involve the sale of assets/ shares/whole business. These agreements include additional clauses. These are regarding the:

  • Employees transfer
  • Intellectual property, and
  • The ongoing obligations of parties after the sale.

Legal Risks and How to Avoid Disputes

The risk of disputes in SPA transactions can arise. Only if the agreement is unclear or incomplete. Sometimes, if not aligned with legal requirements. To avoid these risks:

  • The SPA must be comprehensive. All relevant terms are clearly outlined.
  • Include dispute resolution mechanisms. This includes arbitration.
  • Seek legal advice to ensure compliance. Comply with UAE laws and regulations.

Steps to Execute an SPA in the UAE

  1. Negotiation: Both parties negotiate the agreement terms.
  2. Drafting: A lawyer drafts the SPA. It must cover all necessary clauses.
  3. Signing: Both parties sign the SPA. Done in the presence of a notary or legal witness.
  4. Registration: The SPA must be registered with the relevant authorities for real estate transactions. Examples included the Dubai Land Department.

Amendments and Termination of an SPA

Amendments to the SPA can be made. In case both parties agree in writing. Termination clauses allow either party to cancel the agreement under specified conditions. This includes failure to meet the agreed terms or legal requirements.

Role of Lawyers and Notaries in SPA Transactions

Lawyers have a role in drafting and reviewing the SPA. They guarantee that it complies with UAE laws. Meanwhile, protecting the interests of their clients. For instance, notaries may be involved in witnessing the signing of the agreement. This is particularly true in real estate transactions.

FAQs

Q: Is a SPA legally binding in the UAE?

A: Yes, once signed by both parties, the SPA is legally binding and enforceable under UAE law.

Q: Can I cancel an SPA after signing?

A: Cancellation depends on the termination clauses in the SPA and the mutual agreement of both parties.

Q: Is a notary required for all SPAs?

A: Notarization is generally required for real estate SPAs in the UAE, but not necessarily for other types of agreements.

Conclusion: Ensuring a Secure Transaction with an SPA

A well-drafted SPA provides essential protection for both buyers and sellers. A SPA helps in smooth and secure business and real estate dealings. It can be done by clearly defining the transaction terms. It ensures legal compliance and includes dispute resolution mechanisms. However, always seek legal counsel. Hire someone experienced like Snapsale. Their team ensures that your SPA reflects your interests. While it adheres to local laws.
